_doc: WHERE EACH CHANNEL'S SEQUENTIAL REPEATERS LIVE (docs/physical.md, 'Wrappers and links').

Every block instance sits in a hardening wrapper of the same name (fet, lane_05, ...), and every channel instance runs from its source's wrapper to its destination's. A LINK entry says how many repeater stages (rtl/phys/ccv_common_rpt.sv) each wrapper along that path holds. Any channel instance no entry covers is 'src:0 > dst:0': abutted, no repeaters.
channel  the channel name without ccv_, e.g. fet_dec_instr

copies   which copies of a replicated channel (rcu_lane_ops has 32): "all" (the default), or a list such as [5, 6]. An entry naming copies beats an "all" entry for those copies; any other overlap is an error.

route    the hops, in the direction of valid, as 'wrapper:stages' separated by '>'. It starts at 'src' and ends at 'dst', this copy's own endpoints. Anything between is a FEEDTHROUGH: another wrapper the channel crosses, named by its block instance ('miu', 'lane_06'), which gets ports for it and holds its stages.
why      optional: a note for the reader.
Rules, checked by tools/ccv_links.py whenever the generators run:
- stages are whole numbers, 0 to 16; the end at EXTERNAL holds none (it has no wrapper);
- a route doesn't pass its own endpoints, or any wrapper twice;
- every copy of a lockstep channel has the same total, or lockstep delivery is lost, and the same src stages, since the checker bank watches each link where it leaves the source's wrapper.
- a channel declaring latency_match in the schema (ccv_ooe_fet_ckpt_free, with ccv_ooe_fet_redirect: A-58) has the same total as its partner, so the two arrive in the order they were sent.

What a link's total N changes, derived from this file and nowhere else: its checkers' ROUND_TRIP (+2(N + bnd_rx), and so their DEPTH, the credit loop), TIMEOUT_N (+2(N + bnd_rx)) and SRC_STAGES, and the C++ skeleton's latency and credit depth for that slot (CCV_CREDIT_DEPTH + 2(N + bnd_rx), full bandwidth: Q-43), so both hosts still agree. bnd_rx is 1 where the receiving end holds the boundary flop (no_flop below): in front of a receiver that registers its own inputs and credit, as every DPI host does, it is a stage each way (AR's rev 309 (2)).

hard_reuse: block types whose wrappers must stay hard-reusable. Their instances are grouped by what their wrapper holds -- each end's stages, each feedthrough's channel and stages -- and each group is one TEMPLATE with its stages fixed and no parameters: ccv_<type>_w for the group most instances are in, ccv_<type>_w_v1, _v2, ... for the rest, so a divergent split costs exactly as many templates as it has distinct wrappers, and no more. A type not listed gets one parameterised module (stages set by the top) and a module of its own per instance with feedthroughs.

no_flop: the channel ends built WITHOUT a boundary flop. Every other end's repeater holds one (rtl/phys/ccv_common_rpt.sv, BOUNDARY 1; Daniel, 2026-11-05): the block's own boundary register, built in its wrapper, the sender's last flop or the receiver's first, which CCV_RT_ABUT already counts (AR's rev 285). An entry names a block type (or a list) and "channels": "all" (the default) or a list of channel names without ccv_, with a why. Allowed only where the block's own register drives or takes the port with 0 NGD, which tools/check-ngd.py holds at the block's wrapper, or for a DPI host, whose posedge block is that register (AR's rev 287 (1)). "all" is refused for a block whose top is RTL: an RTL block replacing a stub takes the flops in that same change, never inheriting the stub's no-flop. "except" (with "all" only) leaves the named channels flopped. A receiving end goes zero-cycle only for IPC, measured in a model run of the end flopped against zero-cycle (Daniel, DA-114, 2026-11-06): 0.2% of S1 or less, it stays flopped; over 0.2% and up to 0.5%, Daniel decides; over 0.5%, the block's owner may approve it; an end that cannot meet its 12 NGD port budget without the receiving flop goes to Daniel. A flopped RECEIVING end adds one cycle to its crossing, bnd_rx (AR's revs 300 and 301): a crossing is CCV_LAT_HOP + link_n + bnd_rx, in params/ccv_params.json's derives (bnd_rx('channel')) and in both hosts' links; a flopped sending end adds none, since it replaces the sender's own output register (AR's rev 285). That holds only for an RTL top: a DPI block's posedge block already is its last register, so its sending ends stay no_flop, and a register more there is a link stage, route 'src:1' (AR's rev 309 (1); refused otherwise).

credit_on_receipt: flopped DESTINATION ends whose credit the wrapper returns on receipt (AR's rev 322, RA-41). An entry is {"end": "<channel>@<block type>", "why": ...}. At such an end the boundary stage loads its credit flop from its own valid flop, flop to flop (rtl/phys/ccv_common_rpt.sv CREDIT_ON_RECEIPT): the credit leaves the cycle after the message is presented to the block, as from a block that takes it then, with no second register in series behind the boundary flop for a derive not to count. The block has no credit port on that end (tools/gen-top.py), and CCV_CREDIT_DEPTH keeps its derived value. It is a promise by the block, which the channel's schema entry states as its credit_on_receipt contract: it takes every message the cycle it is presented from the boundary flop, under kill, flush and reset included -- a message landing during a kill is taken and voided, never left or refused -- with no skid of its own, its storage never borrowed from the credit. Refused (tools/ccv_links.py): an end that is not the channel's destination, a zero-cycle end (no_flop: no boundary flop to load from), and an end whose channel carries no such contract; a new end needs a row from its block's architect showing the promise holds there. Checked, not only declared: a block that takes a landed message a cycle late, or drops one, fails both hosts' runs (the receivers' cor_late count, tools/check-kernel.sh and check-sv-hosted.sh); an in-series flop on the credit path fails the full-rate proof (tools/check-formal.sh) and the checker bank's fixed_latency_prompt (tools/check-skel.sh fixed-all).
Example entries (not active):
{"channel": "fet_dec_instr", "route": "src:1 > dst:1"}
{"channel": "dec_ooe_uop",   "route": "src:0 > miu:2 > dst:1", "why": "passes over MIU"}
{"channel": "rcu_lane_ops",  "copies": "all", "route": "src:1 > dst:1"}
{"channel": "rcu_lane_ops",  "copies": [7],   "route": "src:1 > lane_06:1 > dst:0", "why": "lane 7 reached over lane 6"}

no_flop.why: DPI hosts: every block's top is the C++ skeleton over DPI-C (rtl/top/dpi/) or a generated stub, whose posedge block is the boundary register at 0 NGD; dropping it would move both hosts' sampling and gain no contract (AR's rev 287 (1)). Each block leaves this list when its RTL top replaces the stub. RCU is the next entry. OOE leaves it for an entry of its own whose channels are miu_ooe_cmpl and miu_ooe_cmpl_hint only, at bnd_rx 0, taken by OOE's own registers enabled by their valids; every other OOE receiving end takes the boundary flop (OA's ruling C9, re:OI-115, 2026-11-06). Daniel approved C9 (DA-114, 2026-11-06; OA's rev 368 released OA's hold), standing unless OI and OA's rerun at CCV_LAT_LANE 8 / CCV_LAT_SFU 13 shows those two ends recover 0.5% of S1 or less. That entry lands in the same change as ccv_ooe's RTL top, never before: while OOE is a DPI host, leaving this list would flop its sending ends, which a DPI block may not (AR's rev 309 (1)), and every other receiving end in both hosts.

Option 1 (AR's rev 301): RCU puts logic before its first register on these two inputs, so each takes the boundary flop in its wrapper and its crossing counts bnd_rx = 1 (AR's rev 300). lane_rcu_res was a third until RA's rev 95 made its end zero-cycle under DA 114 (LANE 8 to 7, SFU 13 to 12), on two conditions: the block-level read at RCU's assembly holds the end to 12 NGD, or it goes to Daniel; and that link takes no repeater stage, ever, since RCU and the lanes abut. Every other RCU end is taken or driven by a register at 0 NGD, as a DPI host's posedge block is (AR's rev 287 (1)).

credit_on_receipt.why: AR's rev 322 (RA-41): RCU takes every issue the cycle it lands in the boundary flop (RA-41; Credits RCU returns, Done, kill and reset tab), so its credit is that flop's valid a cycle on; rcu_kill's nine credit-pulse flops in series behind the boundary flop, a register no derive counts, go.

AR's rev 322 (RA-41): RCU takes every load return the cycle it lands in the boundary flop, so its credit is that flop's valid a cycle on; rcu_kill's four MIU credit-pulse flops go. lane_rcu_res stays zero-cycle, with rcu_kill's 32 (AR's rev 322 (c)).
